detailZh: Alexa Rendell在巴西圣保罗大奖赛前加入天空体育F1团队
Alexa Rendell已在本周末巴西圣保罗大奖赛前加入天空体育F1团队；圣保罗大奖赛周五练习赛将于下午3点30分和晚上7点在天空体育F1频道直播
天空体育任命Alexa Rendell为F1多媒体记者，进一步增强了其屡获殊荣的一级方程式团队，这家广播机构希望让更多车迷更贴近这项运动。
在一个新设立的职位上，Alexa将在天空体育的社交渠道、一级方程式直播节目和天空体育新闻中工作，让车迷更贴近那些使一级方程式成为世界上最引人入胜的运动之一的人物、故事和时刻。
她的任命正值一级方程式赛车持续吸引更广泛、更多元化的观众之际，年轻车迷和女性在这项运动的增长中扮演着越来越重要的角色。自2012年成为一级方程式赛车在英国和爱尔兰的转播主场以来，天空体育的35岁以下观众增长了120%，女性观众则翻了一倍多。2025赛季也是天空体育历史上收视率最高的赛季。

Alexa 将帮助延续这一势头，制作能够反映车迷欣赏和参与一级方程式赛车方式不断演变的内容，同时让这项运动更易于接触，并拉近观众与赛事的距离。从围场里最重大的新闻，到比赛周末之外的人物个性与竞争关系，她将在联系资深车迷和首次接触这项运动的人群方面发挥重要作用。
作为其职责的一部分，Alexa 将在整个一级方程式围场以及天空体育的直播报道中进行报道，采访车手、车队领队以及这项运动中的其他关键人物。她将随天空体育 F1 团队前往巴西参加即将到来的大奖赛，并在那里开始拉近车迷与赛事的距离。
一级方程式多媒体记者 Alexa Rendell 表示：“我非常激动能加入天空体育 F1 大家庭。一级方程式一直是我的初恋，而天空体育从我十几岁起就是我在这项运动中旅程的一部分，当时我通过其体验活动第一次接触到这个行业。如今能加入这个团队，感觉真是一个特别圆满的时刻。”
“我迫不及待想从巴西开始投入工作，讲述让这项运动如此不可思议的故事。随着新一代车迷进入这项运动，我非常期待帮助与这些观众建立联系，并以新鲜而引人入胜的方式分享 F1。”
天空体育F1总监比利·麦金蒂表示：“我们非常高兴欢迎亚历克莎加入团队。她是赛车运动转播领域的一颗冉冉升起的新星，拥有与观众建立联系的本能。一级方程式正在不断发展，越来越多的人开始发现并接触这项运动，我们的报道也必须与时俱进——寻找新的方式来讲述故事，让车迷更贴近那些让F1如此引人入胜的人物和时刻。”
亚历克莎加入天空体育时，已拥有创作者、记者和主持人的丰富经验，涉猎广泛的赛车运动，包括电动方程式、国际汽联世界耐力锦标赛、Extreme E和F1学院。
天空体育近期与一级方程式达成了一项新的长期合作伙伴关系，巩固了其作为该运动在英国和爱尔兰的大本营的地位，直至2034赛季结束。在英国和爱尔兰，天空体育和NOW是唯一可以观看每节练习赛、排位赛、冲刺赛和大奖赛直播的地方。

detailEn: Alexa Rendell joins Sky Sports F1 team ahead of Sao Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil

Alexa Rendell has joined the Sky Sports F1 team ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Sao Paulo GP from 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1
Sky Sports has strengthened its award-winning Formula 1 team with the appointment of Alexa Rendell as F1 Multimedia Journalist, as the broadcaster looks to bring even more fans closer to the sport.

In a newly created role, Alexa will work across Sky Sports' social channels, live Formula 1 programming and Sky Sports News, bringing fans closer to the personalities, stories, and moments that make Formula 1 one of the world's most compelling sports.

Her appointment comes as Formula 1 continues to attract a broader and more diverse audience, with younger fans and women playing an increasingly important part in the sport's growth. Since becoming the home of Formula 1 in the UK and Ireland in 2012, Sky Sports has seen viewing among under-35s increase by 120 per cent, while its female audience has more than doubled. The 2025 season was also the most-watched in Sky Sports' history.

Alexa will help build on that momentum, creating content that reflects the evolving ways fans enjoy and engage with Formula 1, while making the sport more accessible and bringing audiences closer to the action. From the biggest stories in the paddock, to the personalities and rivalries beyond the race weekend, she will play an important role in connecting with both established fans and those discovering the sport for the first time.

As part of her role, Alexa will report from across the Formula 1 paddock and Sky Sports' live coverage, interviewing drivers, team principals, and other key figures from across the sport. She will join the Sky Sports F1 team in Brazil for the upcoming Grand Prix, where she will begin bringing fans closer to the action.

Alexa Rendell, F1 Multimedia Journalist, said: "I'm really thrilled to be joining the Sky Sports F1 family. Formula 1 has always been my first love, and Sky has been part of my journey in the sport since I was a teenager, when I got my first taste of the industry through its access events. To now be joining the team feels like a really special full-circle moment.

"I can't wait to get stuck in from Brazil and tell the stories that make this sport so incredible. With a new generation of fans coming into the sport, I'm really looking forward to helping connect with those audiences and sharing F1 in fresh and engaging ways."

Billy McGinty, Director of F1 at Sky Sports, said: "We're delighted to welcome Alexa to the team. She is a rising star in motorsport broadcasting and has an instinct for connecting with audiences. Formula 1 is evolving, with more people than ever discovering and connecting with the sport, and it's important that our coverage evolves too - finding new ways to tell the stories and bring fans closer to the personalities and moments that make F1 so compelling."
Alexa joins Sky Sports with experience as a creator, reporter, and presenter across a broad range of motorsport, including Formula E, the FIA World Endurance Championship, Extreme E, and F1 Academy.

Sky recently agreed a new long-term partnership with Formula 1, securing its position as the home of the sport in the UK and Ireland until the end of the 2034 season. In the UK and Ireland, Sky and NOW are the only places to watch live coverage of every practice, qualifying session, Sprint, and Grand Prix.

items.originalTitle: Charles Leclerc welcomes first child with wife Alexandra as couple shares baby news
detailZh: 查尔斯·勒克莱尔与妻子亚历山德拉迎来第一个孩子，夫妇俩分享育儿喜讯
查尔斯·勒克莱尔及其妻子亚历山德拉迎来了他们的第一个孩子
查尔斯·勒克莱尔，法拉利，亚历山德拉·勒克莱尔
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计以及那些让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事。
法拉利一级方程式车手查尔斯·勒克莱尔和他的妻子亚历山德拉·勒克莱尔迎来了他们的第一个孩子。
这对夫妇于2026年2月在摩纳哥举行了一场私人婚礼，他们在社交媒体上宣布了这个新生命的到来。他们分享了一张新生儿的腿和脚穿着粉色针织裤和白色袜子照片，并配文：“Bianca. 3.11.26。”
在墨西哥大奖赛结束第四名后，勒克莱尔在即将到来的巴西大奖赛之前飞回了摩纳哥。
摩纳哥车手最近在接受《哈珀斯杂志》采访时谈到了成为父亲的经历，他形容这“非常、非常特别”，然后补充说：“我非常期待。”
他继续说：“我们已经有了一个儿子，那就是Leo，因为我们已经把他当作儿子看待，再次成为父母将是一件很棒的事情。”
当被问及场外他的优先事项时，这位29岁的车手解释说：“和我的妻子、Leo、我的家人和朋友们共度时光。这可能是我在有空闲时间时尝试做的最重要的事情，因为这样的空闲时间并不常见。”
“这种平衡本身就是很自然的，因为首要任务是所有场上的活动以及任何能让我作为车手变得更好以及我们作为团队能做得更好的事情。然后，剩下的时间，我用来投入到我喜欢的项目中。”
这个宣布在粉丝和F1围场内的其他人中引起了很大的反响。
“为你感到非常高兴。欢迎来到这个世界，比安卡，”勒克莱尔的前队友卡洛斯·塞恩斯写道，而麦克拉伦的奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂补充道：“恭喜你们俩！”
“向你们俩表示衷心的祝贺！！这是好消息，”法拉利F1车队评论道，而梅赛德斯也发布了：“欢迎来到这个世界，比安卡！向你们所有人表示衷心的祝贺。”
detailEn: Charles Leclerc welcomes first child with wife Alexandra as couple shares baby news
Charles Leclerc and his wife Alexandra have welcomed their first child
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Alexandra Leclerc
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
Ferrari Formula 1 driver Charles Leclerc and his wife, Alexandra Leclerc, have welcomed their first child together.

The couple, who tied the knot in a private Monaco ceremony in February 2026, announced the new arrival on social media. They shared a photo of the newborn’s legs and feet in pink knitted leggings and white socks with the caption, “Bianca. 3.11.26.”
After finishing fourth at the Mexican Grand Prix, Leclerc flew home to Monaco before the Brazilian Grand Prix this coming weekend.
The Monegasque driver recently opened up on becoming a father during an interview with Harper’s Bazaar, describing it as "very, very special", before adding: "I’m just really looking forward to it."
He continued: "We already have one son in Leo, because we already consider him as a son, and it will be great to become a parent for a second time."

When asked what his priorities are away from the racetrack, the 29-year-old explained: "Spending time with my wife, with Leo, with my family and my friends. This is probably the number one thing I try and do whenever I’ve got free time, because it’s not so often that we get it.

"The balance is very natural in itself, because the priority remains all the on-track activity and whatever makes me better as a driver and what we can do better as a team. Then, whatever is left, I spend it on the projects I enjoy."
The announcement drew a big reaction from fans and others within the F1 paddock.
"So happy for you. Welcome to the world Bianca," Leclerc's former team-mate Carlos Sainz wrote, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri added: "Congrats to you both!"
"Huge congratulations to you both!! Wonderful news," the Ferrari F1 team commented, while Mercedes also posted: "Welcome to the world, Bianca! Huge congratulations to you all."

items.originalTitle: Max Verstappen needs "a conversation" with Red Bull engine after "random" engine braking issues
detailZh: 维斯塔潘需要在红牛引擎后进行一次"谈话"，因为出现了"随机"的引擎制动问题
尽管红牛福特动力系统在高海拔地区通过了首次测试，并以优异的成绩完成，但维斯塔潘认为仍有改进的空间
在阿特奥多罗·赫尔曼诺斯·罗德里格斯赛道（海拔2,286米，是F1赛历中海拔最高的赛道）的比赛周末之前，车队的讨论主要集中在一个问题：墨西哥城对2026年动力单元将构成多大的挑战
几家制造商担心严重的涡轮迟滞，尤其是在MGU-H不再支持涡轮的情况下。较低的空气密度也引发了一个关于绝对性能的关键问题。在高海拔地区，每立方米的氧气分子数量更少，这意味着涡轮需要更努力地工作，才能将与海平面相同的氧气量送入发动机。
本田首席工程师奥里哈拉在周四已经解释说，如果一个制造商在高海拔地区无法产生足够的涡轮增压，这将影响"发动机运行条件"，换句话说，就是内燃机可以提供的绝对动力。
尽管这对于所有制造商来说都是F1新规则下的未知因素，但作为新来者之一，红牛福特动力系统实际上正面临其在高海拔地区的首次考验。
根据车队负责人劳伦特·梅基斯的说法，这是一次团队以优异成绩通过的测试，也许甚至有些令人惊讶。
"听着，你说的没错，墨西哥是一个例外，它提出了一个非常、非常独特的挑战。从动力单元的角度来看，显然它运行得很好。所以，向这些家伙表示巨大的祝贺和恭喜，"梅基斯在Motorsport.com询问他关于墨西哥高海拔地区的动力单元挑战后说。
"在底盘方面，它也表现良好，因为底盘上有许多挑战，比如汽车冷却、刹车冷却以及许多其他事情。”
"我们知道在墨西哥看到的任何东西都只能被视为一次性的。我们只是不知道我们会享受到竞争优势还是竞争劣势。但结果证明，我们处于正确的组合中。”
"尽管如此，马克斯·维斯塔潘认为DM01，红牛的第一个内部制造的动力单元，仍有几个改进的领域。其中之一就是发动机制动。在奥斯汀，这已经让这位四次世界冠军在驾驶中感到不稳定，而在墨西哥，维斯塔潘再次通过车队无线电抱怨了这一点。”
"这是随机发生的"
“说实话，发动机自己决定要做什么，所以我也不知道。也许我需要在比赛前和发动机聊一聊。也许它需要表现得更好。” 维斯塔潘 开玩笑地说。
“我们不知道，有时候事情就是会发生。它并不非常一致。但我认为这里的一切都运行得太热了，包括涡轮增压器等一切，所以很难让一切都恰到好处。”
红牛找到什么来改善它的起步了吗？
虽然发动机制动的稳定性仍然是需要改进的领域，但也许是红牛最大的积极因素是它在墨西哥的起步出奇地好。维斯塔潘 和 哈贾尔 在资格赛后都表达了一些担忧，尤其是由于通往第 1 弯的极端长距离，但在实践中事情的结果比预期的要好得多。
查尔斯·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利，马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队
据梅基斯所说，这表明红牛车队在发车方面正在稳步进步，尽管他还不希望就此过于乐观。红牛车队的车队经理知道，在下个赛季到来之前，还需要更多的硬件改动。
“情况是这样的，我们知道我们不是标杆。在米尔顿凯恩斯，我们正在进行大量工作，以改善我们今年所拥有的发车表现，”梅基斯在被问及Motorsport.com报道的令人惊讶的强劲发车表现时说。
“是的，你们已经看到了一些进步，尤其是在今天的高压条件下，因为我们有几次发车要处理，而且是在那个非常长的通往第1弯的直道上，一切都被放大了。”
"围绕这有很多压力和关注，我为他们今天能给我们最好的表现感到非常自豪。"
"这意味着我们现在是标杆吗？不。这意味着我们将在每一场比赛中都有一个完美的开始，或者像今天这样的开始吗？不。但它确实意味着我们将继续努力，用我们拥有的东西来提高。"
detailEn: Max Verstappen needs "a conversation" with Red Bull engine after "random" engine braking issues
Although Red Bull Ford Powertrains passed its first test at high altitude with flying colours, Verstappen believes there are still areas for improvement

Ahead of the race weekend at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez – at 2,286 metres above sea level, by far the highest circuit on the Formula 1 calendar – the discussion in the paddock largely revolved around one subject: how much of a challenge Mexico City would pose for the 2026 power units.

Several manufacturers feared severe turbo lag, especially now that the MGU-H is no longer there to support the turbo. The lower air density also raised a crucial question regarding outright performance. At altitude, there are fewer oxygen molecules per cubic metre, meaning the turbo has to work harder to get the same amount of oxygen into the engine as it would at sea level.

Honda chief engineer Shintaro Orihara had already explained on Thursday that if a manufacturer cannot generate sufficient turbo boost at altitude, it would have consequences for the "engine operation condition", in other words, the outright power the internal combustion engine can deliver.
Although this was an unknown for all manufacturers under F1’s new regulations, Red Bull Ford Powertrains, as one of the newcomers, was literally facing its first baptism of fire at high altitude.
It was a test that, according to team principal Laurent Mekies, the team passed with flying colours, perhaps even surprisingly so.

"Look, you're right in saying that Mexico is an exception that presents a very, very unique challenge. Power unit wise, obviously it has worked well. So a huge well done and congrats to the guys", Mekies said after Motorsport.com asked him about the power unit challenge at Mexico’s altitude.
"Also on the chassis side, it has also worked well, because you have a very large number of challenges on the chassis as well for the car cooling, for the brakes cooling, and for many other things.

"We knew that whatever we were going to see in Mexico would be to be considered as a one-off. We just didn't know if we were going to enjoy a competitive advantage or a competitive disadvantage. But as it turned out, we were in the right mix."

Nevertheless, Max Verstappen believes there are still several areas for improvement with the DM01, Red Bull’s first in-house built power unit. One of those is the engine braking. In Austin, this had already given the four-time world champion an inconsistent feeling behind the wheel, and in Mexico Verstappen once again complained about it over the team radio.
"It happens randomly", the Dutchman later explained in the post-race press conference.

"The engine just decides by itself what to do, to be honest, so I don't know. Maybe I need to have a conversation with the engine before going into the race. Maybe it has to behave better", Verstappen joked.
"We don't know, sometimes it just happens. It's not very consistent. But I think everything is running so hot here, also the turbocharger and everything, so it's tough to make everything spot on."
Has Red Bull found something to improve its starts?

While consistency with engine braking remains an area for improvement, perhaps the biggest positive for Red Bull was that its starts in Mexico were surprisingly good. Both Verstappen and Isack Hadjar had expressed some concerns about them after qualifying, particularly because of the extremely long run to Turn 1, but in practice things turned out much better than feared.
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing

According to Mekies, this underlines that Red Bull is steadily making progress with its starts, although he does not want to get carried away just yet. Red Bull’s team principal knows that more significant hardware changes will still be needed heading into next season.

"The situation is that we know we are not benchmark. There is a huge amount of work going on in Milton Keynes to improve the starts with what we have this year", Mekies said when asked about the surprisingly strong starts by Motorsport.com.
"And yes, you've seen some of this progress, certainly under high stress conditions today, because we had several starts to make with that very long stretch to Turn 1 where everything is amplified.
"There is a huge amount of pressure and attention around it and I'm very proud of how they managed to give us the best we could today.

"Does it mean we are now the benchmark? No. Does it mean that we will have a perfect start or a start like today in every race? No. But it does mean that we will continue to try and improve with what we have."

items.originalTitle: Why Daniel Ricciardo is staying away from the F1 paddock
items.summaryEn: Daniel Ricciardo has explained why he has been staying away from the Formula 1 paddock. His F1 career ended after the 2024 Singapore Grand Prix, when RB replaced him with Liam Lawson.
detailZh: 丹尼尔·里卡多解释了自己为何一直远离F1围场。
里卡多的F1生涯结束后，他便退出了公众视野。以下是他为何不确定自己是否还想回来的原因。
一名车迷举着丹尼尔·里卡多的标语牌。
丹尼尔·里卡多详细讲述了自己一直远离F1围场的原因。
里卡多的F1生涯在2024年新加坡大奖赛之后结束，当时这位小红牛车手在经历了一个艰难的赛季后被利亚姆·劳森取代。
过去两年里，这位澳大利亚人远离了聚光灯，更多时间待在家里，更少乘坐飞机，不过他确实成为了福特赛车的全球大使。
并非所有前F1车手在停止参加世界锦标赛后都保持不活跃。其中一些人在其他系列赛中比赛；在2025年和2026年，罗伯特·库比卡、小林可梦伟和尼克·德弗里斯赢得了勒芒24小时耐力赛。
其他人则成为电视评论员，比如简森·巴顿、大卫·库特哈德、海基·科瓦莱宁、尼科·罗斯伯格和雅克·维伦纽夫等众多人士。
里卡多尚未涉足这些，当在《Beyond The Grid》播客中被问及我们是否会以某种身份看到他重返F1围场时，这位八次大奖赛冠军得主回应道：“我不确定。
“如果你一年前问我，我会说‘不，我再也不想只是待在周围了’。那时，我感受到很多痛苦，所以待在周围会带来太多痛苦。我对此非常消极。
“但我觉得过去几年我也试着理解我的自尊心。当所有这些事情发生并在你面前崩塌时，会有一些感觉，我猜，像是自尊心的死亡。然后我想，为什么我这么反对？好吧，那也是我的自尊心在说话，‘哦，我永远不会回到围场，我不想见那些人’，那大概也是我的自尊心在试图保护我自己。
“我现在处于一个非常感激F1给予我的许多东西以及那些关系的位置；我仍然和很多车手、工程师、机械师交谈——有些关系我仍然保持着。甚至新加坡[2024]，比赛后那晚我在赛道待得很晚，因为我知道，我当时想，我不知道什么时候会回来。所以我尽量多地道别，但非常伤感，只是可能不是我想和某些人道别的方式。”

“所以我确实想回去，但让我纠结的是，如果我回去得太早，会不会就变成‘嘿，丹尼尔，他是不是要回来了，他在干什么？’我不想背负那种媒体包袱，我只想去见见一些朋友，但我也明白F1围场不是那样的，运作方式也不是那样——这一点我理解。这也是我一直没回去的原因之一，因为我不想要那种关注，我觉得如果我没有明确目的就走进围场，那就会变成‘好吧，丹尼尔为什么在这儿，他是不是就为了拍张照片？’这些只是我对自己说的话，”他笑着说。
“我真的不想到处奔波。一想到F1的赛历我就发怵，所以这就是我的想法，我觉得那里没有什么是我会……”
“我跟几个朋友聊过，他们在其他运动项目里，现在是退役运动员，但以管理者、车队老板的身份回到了这项运动，或者担任了某个角色。说来有趣。其中一位特别说过，‘这并不比我参赛时轻松’，因为你仍然投入得那么深——尤其是对运动员——他们的问题就是你的问题，而且你下班回家也摆脱不了。你仍然背负着一名运动员的重量。”
“我确实喜欢和年轻车手交流，我确实喜欢尝试分享我的一些知识和经验。我只是觉得我不想再经历所有这些情绪了——那太沉重了。想到能脱离那些，活得更轻松、更自由一点，那感觉就是更好、更舒服。”
“我不认为那能帮助我成为最好的自己，尤其是在对我重要的人身边。”
这位珀斯本地人一直在电视上看比赛，他的父亲很欣赏他的见解。那么他是否愿意有朝一日当评论员呢？“还有出差奔波呢！”里卡多惊呼道。
丹尼尔·里卡多、格蕾丝·里卡多、乔·里卡多
“这很难，因为很多人对我说，‘哦，你在电视上会很出色’。你看，我内心有一部分觉得，是的，能分享我的许多经验和知识会很棒。即使我和我爸爸一起看比赛，我爸爸也会说，‘天哪，得有人听听你在比赛期间说的话，因为我看比赛时从你那里学到了很多’。显然那只是因为我是那20名车手之一。我想，我们中有少数人真正体验过那种水平。显然我很感激很多前车手现在从事那个领域，这是有原因的。
“人生中做些完全不同的事情，也有一种令人耳目一新的感觉。也许能以某种方式活出两段人生，光是这个想法就挺美好的。也许就是合上那本书、继续前行，听起来也很酷。但有时候我又会想，我拥有35年的赛车智慧和知识；就这样把它锁进盒子里，再也不让人看到或听到，这算不算一种浪费？
“我不知道。我想这就是为什么我还没有真正投入任何事情，因为我在努力确保我所做的是对的。”
detailEn: Why Daniel Ricciardo is staying away from the F1 paddock
Ricciardo stepped away from the limelight when his F1 career ended. Here’s why he’s unsure he even wants to come back
A fan holds up a sign of Daniel Ricciardo
Daniel Ricciardo has delved into the reasons why he has been staying away from the Formula 1 paddock.
Ricciardo’s F1 career ended after the 2024 Singapore Grand Prix, when the RB driver was replaced by Liam Lawson after enduring a tough campaign thus far.
In the past two years, the Australian has stayed away from the limelight, spending more time at home and less on planes, though he did become a global ambassador for Ford Racing.

Not all former F1 drivers stay inactive when they stop competing in the world championship. Some of them race in other series; across 2025 and 2026, Robert Kubica, Kamui Kobayashi and Nyck de Vries won the Le Mans 24 Hours.
Others become TV pundits, like Jenson Button, David Coulthard, Heikki Kovalainen, Nico Rosberg and Jacques Villeneuve among many others.

Ricciardo has engaged in none of this yet, and when asked in the Beyond The Grid podcast if we would see him back in the F1 paddock in some capacity, the eight-time grand prix winner responded: “I’m not sure.

“If you would have asked me a year ago, I would have said ‘No, I don’t ever want to just be around anymore’. At that time, I felt a lot of pain, so it caused too much pain to be around. I was very negative towards it.

“But I think also the last couple of years I’ve tried to understand my ego. There were some feelings of, I guess, like an ego death, when all of these things happen and kind of collapse in front of you. Then I was like, why am I so anti? Okay, that’s my ego also talking, ‘Oh, I’m never going to come back to the paddock, I don’t want to see any of those people’, and that’s also probably my ego trying to protect myself.

“I’m at a place now where I’m very appreciative of many of the things that F1 gave me and the relationships too; I still speak to a lot of the drivers, engineers, mechanics – there’s relationships that I still have. Even Singapore [2024], I stayed at the track quite late that night after the race, because I knew, I was like, I don’t know when I’m going to be back. So I tried to say as many goodbyes as I could, but it was very sombre, just not the way I probably want to say goodbye to some people.

“So I do want to, but I think the thing I’ve been torn with is if I go back too soon, is it just going to be like, ‘Hey, Daniel, is he coming back, what is he doing?’. I don’t want the kind of media baggage with that, I just want to be able to go and see some friends, but I also appreciate that’s not the reality of an F1 paddock and how it works – and I understand that. It’s kind of why I haven’t come back as well, because I don’t want the attention, and I think if I go into the paddock without a purpose, it’s like, ‘Okay, why is Daniel here, is he just looking to get his photo taken?’. These are just things I tell myself,” he chuckled.
“I don’t really want to travel. The thought of the F1 calendar freaks me out, so that’s where I’m like, I don’t think there’s anything there that I would…

“I spoke to a few friends, in other sports, that are now retired athletes but went back into the sport as a manager, as a team owner, or taken a role. It’s funny. One of them in particular said, ‘It’s no easier than when I was competing’, because you still are so invested – especially in the athletes – that their problems are your problems, and you don’t get home from work. You’re still living with the weight of an athlete.

“I do love speaking with younger drivers and I do love trying to share some of my knowledge and experiences. I just don’t think I want to go through all those emotions again – it’s a lot. The thought of just being out of that and living a little more lightly, freely, that just feels nicer and better.
“I don’t think that would help me be maybe the best version of myself, especially around people that matter to me.”
The Perth native has been watching races on TV, with his father enjoying his insight. So might he enjoy being a pundit sometime? “The travel!” Ricciardo exclaimed.
Daniel Ricciardo, Grace Ricciardo, Joe Ricciardo

“It’s hard, because a lot of people tell me, ‘Oh, you’d be great on TV’. Look, there’s a part of me that, yes, it would be awesome to share many of my experiences and knowledge. Even if I watch a race with, even my dad, my dad is like, ‘Man, someone has to hear what you have to say during a race, because I learn so much from you when I watch a race’. Obviously that’s just because I was one of the 20. There’s, I guess, a few of us who have really experienced it to that level. Obviously I appreciate a lot of ex-drivers are in that space now, there’s a reason for that.

“There’s just also something refreshing about doing something completely different with life. Being able to live maybe two lives, in a way, the thought of that is also really quite nice. Maybe just closing that book and moving on, that also sounds cool. But then there’s times where I’m like, I have 35 years of racing wisdom and knowledge; to just kind of lock it in a box and never let it be seen or heard, is that a waste?
“I don’t know. I think that’s why I haven’t really jumped on anything, because I’m trying to make sure what I do is right.”
keyPointsZh: 里卡多表示，他不确定自己是否还想回到F1围场
keyPointsEn: Ricciardo said he is unsure whether he even wants to come back to the F1 paddock
